product.name: Zentrik Open CRM
product.type: Open-source customer relationship and product-feedback CRM
product.mission: Help small product teams remember what matters, act on the next right thing, and turn trustworthy feedback into better product decisions.
product.description: An open, local-first CRM for keeping account memory, customer evidence, next actions, and product learning connected so humans and CLI agents can move from signal to useful work without losing provenance.
product.descriptionAnalysis: The product boundary includes account and contact memory, pipeline and tasks, source-grounded feedback, agent handoff, and a public-safe product-evolution loop. It does not store private customer data in the public repository and does not turn unmoderated feedback into roadmap commitments.
product.stack: Vite, React, TypeScript, Tailwind, browser persistence, portable exports, and CLI-agent workflows

contextUnits.name: Product promise and boundaries
contextUnits.description: The product contract: what Open CRM is for, who it serves, and what it deliberately does not claim.
contextUnits.data:
# Product promise and boundaries

Zentrik Open CRM is a local-first, open CRM for keeping account memory, customer evidence, next actions, and product learning connected. It should help a small team move from a trustworthy signal to a useful action without losing provenance.

## In scope
- Account and contact memory
- Pipeline, tasks, notes, and next actions
- Source-grounded feedback and moderation
- Human and CLI-agent handoff
- Product ideas, releases, and outcome checks

## Out of scope
- A replacement for a production ERP, billing system, or security incident system
- Unmoderated roadmap automation
- Private customer data in the public repository
- Treating an agent proposal as a human decision

contextUnits.name: Core entity model
contextUnits.description: Definitions for the records that make the CRM legible to people and agents.
contextUnits.data:
# Core entity model

- **Account:** a company, community, or working relationship with durable context.
- **Contact:** a person associated with an account and a relationship role.
- **Signal:** a source-grounded observation, request, issue, review, or research record.
- **Idea:** a reviewed product possibility that preserves its supporting evidence.
- **Task:** an accountable next action with an owner, status, and due context.
- **Feature:** a user-facing product capability, organized by workflow.
- **Release:** a record of what changed and why.
- **Outcome:** a check of whether the intended user or business result changed.

Facts, interpretations, decisions, and assumptions must remain distinguishable.

contextUnits.name: First-run onboarding
contextUnits.description: The shortest path from install to first value and the information a new operator must understand.
contextUnits.data:
# First-run onboarding

The first session should guide a new operator through: choose demo or empty mode, define the working boundary, create or import one account, capture one source-grounded signal, inspect account memory, choose one next action, and hand one bounded task to an agent.

The UI should explain local browser persistence, export and reset, synthetic demo data, and the difference between browser state and the CLI snapshot.

contextUnits.name: Human and agent operating contract
contextUnits.description: Rules for safe, useful collaboration between humans and CLI agents.
contextUnits.data:
# Human and agent operating contract

Humans own product intent, prioritization, customer communication, privacy decisions, and publication. Agents may inspect the explicit workspace snapshot, research within the stated boundary, draft proposals, change repository files when asked, run validation, and report evidence.

Every agent handoff should state scope, source records, intended outcome, acceptance criteria, allowed writes, and unresolved questions. Agents must not invent customer facts, publish private material, or silently convert a proposal into a commitment.

contextUnits.name: Evidence and provenance rules
contextUnits.description: The minimum source and confidence information required before a signal can influence product work.
contextUnits.data:
# Evidence and provenance rules

A signal should retain a stable external identity where available, source type, source URL, capture time, privacy route, product or account link, and a short statement of what is directly observed.

A single repeated account is not multiple independent sources. Distinguish direct user evidence, public research, internal hypothesis, and synthetic fixture data. Do not claim demand, severity, or outcome without supporting evidence.

contextUnits.name: Privacy and moderation
contextUnits.description: Public-safe handling rules for private, public, synthetic, and security-sensitive material.
contextUnits.data:
# Privacy and moderation

Default to private. Keep credentials, personal data, private support content, security reports, internal relationship notes, and unreviewed customer evidence out of public artifacts.

The public Buildroom may contain only moderated, source-safe summaries. GitHub is a public engineering record when the reporter chooses that path; Zentrik can hold the structured signal and backlink. Security issues always use the private security path.

contextUnits.name: Feedback routing and GitHub
contextUnits.description: How inputs move from channels into a coherent, reviewable evidence loop.
contextUnits.data:
# Feedback routing and GitHub

- Private in-app or hosted feedback becomes a private Signal.
- Buildroom submissions become public candidates only after moderation.
- GitHub Issues remain the public engineering record and may be mirrored as Signals with stable links.
- Support material remains private and can create a triage Task.

Each imported record must preserve the originating URL, source system, stable external ID, privacy decision, and the product/workflow area it concerns.

contextUnits.name: Release and outcome loop
contextUnits.description: The operating loop that makes the product self-evolving without allowing automatic roadmap drift.
contextUnits.data:
# Release and outcome loop

Signal -> review -> Insight or problem pattern -> Opportunity or Idea -> human decision -> implementation task -> Release -> Outcome check.

The loop is complete only when the shipped change is checked against the intended user or business outcome. Preserve rejected and deferred decisions as history; do not delete them to make the workspace look clean.

contextUnits.name: Integration identity and API operations
contextUnits.description: Stable identity and credential rules for future repository and source-system wiring.
contextUnits.data:
# Integration identity and API operations

Use `zentrik-open-crm` as the stable product external ID. Use stable source namespaces and external IDs for imported Signals, Ideas, and Opportunities so retries update rather than duplicate.

The dedicated workspace key is a scoped, revocable secret. Keep it outside the repository and browser localStorage, use the smallest required scopes, never print it, and rotate it when ownership or exposure changes.

contextUnits.name: Launch readiness and support
contextUnits.description: The checks and support path that must be true before a public user relies on the CRM.
contextUnits.data:
# Launch readiness and support

Before launch, verify that a new user can install or open the app, understand local persistence, choose demo or empty mode, create or import an account, capture a signal, choose a next action, export a backup, and hand work to a CLI agent.

Support should collect reproducible steps, environment, privacy route, and source links. Public issues belong in GitHub when safe; private support and security reports stay private. Every release should name known limitations and the next feedback path.

contextUnits.name: Repository wiring contract
contextUnits.description: The boundary between the public Open CRM repository and the Zentrik workspace of record.
contextUnits.data:
# Repository wiring contract

The repository owns the local-first UI, synthetic fixtures, portable schemas, and agent-facing instructions. Zentrik owns the connected product context, source-grounded Signals, reviewed Discovery records, and workspace audit trail.

The repository may send approved, public-safe envelopes using stable external IDs. It must never commit workspace keys, private records, session tokens, or customer data. A sync failure must be visible and recoverable; it must not silently drop evidence.

contextUnits.name: GitHub intake and issue hygiene
contextUnits.description: Rules for turning public repository activity into useful, deduplicated product evidence.
contextUnits.data:
# GitHub intake and issue hygiene

Use GitHub for reproducible bugs, setup friction, documentation gaps, and contributor work. Preserve the issue URL, repository, issue number, author-visible wording, labels, timestamps, and a stable source external ID.

Do not import every comment as a separate demand signal. Deduplicate by issue identity, separate maintainer discussion from user evidence, and keep security reports on the private security route.

contextUnits.name: Buildroom moderation operations
contextUnits.description: The review path from public feedback candidate to safe community-facing request.
contextUnits.data:
# Buildroom moderation operations

A Buildroom candidate is not a roadmap commitment. A human moderator checks privacy, source accuracy, duplicate status, scope, and whether the summary preserves the reporter's intent before publication.

Record the moderation decision and reason. Keep rejected, deferred, and merged candidates as history. Public votes or requests express demand; they do not replace source evidence or product judgment.

contextUnits.name: Public launch boundary
contextUnits.description: The explicit conditions for opening the CRM to outside users while keeping trust and safety intact.
contextUnits.data:
# Public launch boundary

Launch only when a clean install has a reliable first-use path, synthetic demo data is safe, export and reset work, agent snapshots are understandable, and feedback routes explain public versus private handling.

Publish known limitations and a support path. Do not call the CRM production-ready until persistence, sync failure recovery, secret handling, and the moderation boundary have been exercised in a disposable validation workspace.

contextUnits.name: Support triage and feedback loop
contextUnits.description: The operational loop for turning user questions and failures into recoverable work and product learning.
contextUnits.data:
# Support triage and feedback loop

Capture the user's goal, exact steps, expected result, actual result, environment, privacy route, and source links. Classify the report as question, setup friction, defect, request, or security issue before linking it to a product area.

Close the loop with a response, a task or issue when needed, and an outcome check. Keep support records private unless the user intentionally moves a safe summary to a public channel.
